title: The meta cleavage of catechol by Azotobacter species. 4-Oxalocrotonate pathway.

material_comparisons.finding: Paper presents six steps through the oxidative branch to acetaldehyde and pyruvate; it does not establish the seventh acetyl-CoA-producing step. The current five-step hydrolytic formal route is a different explicitly bounded route.

Very low, noninducible hydrolytic activity is measured in named Azotobacter extracts; oxidative dehydrogenation is inferred dominant. Current record has no Azotobacter occurrence or catalyst claims, and native listed taxa are not presented as universal whole-route experimental proof.

Decarboxylase/hydratase activities are not resolved; the transient intermediate has historical keto nomenclature. This paper does not establish the current exact 2Z enol reaction or purified hydratase identity.
Partially purified extract gives acetaldehyde and pyruvate from synthetic hydroxy-oxo substrate; no exact S assignment is independently established by these preparations.

Generalizing a hydrolytic route to every meta-cleaving Pseudomonas strain is explicitly questioned. Current record already separates formal route identity from organism-level proof and retains the oxidative branch as adjacent context.

verdict: No material contradiction to current next261 biological assertions and no new blocking finding.
